Airborne transmission represents a significant factor in the global spread of respiratory infectious diseases, a concern that has intensified due to the coronavirus pandemic. This paper introduces a quasi-well-mixed framework designed to simulate the inhalation exposure of infectious aerosols within confined, small-to-medium indoor spaces. This approach extends the classical Kappa-quasi well-mixed framework by incorporating a spatially explicit "well-mixedness" index derived from experimental airflow and concentration data. The proposed framework was validated through comparisons with results from a high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics model, demonstrating strong alignment in predicted infection risks across various scenarios, including changes in room dimensions, airflow patterns, and host movement. Additionally, the utility of this quasi-well-mixed approach for forecasting disease transmission on urban buses was examined. The results indicate that incompact urban transit environments, the framework yields estimates closely matching those of detailed CFD simulations, thereby establishing its effectiveness in predicting illness spread in such settings.

The concept of market fairness has gained significant traction in the research community, primarily driven by the desire to ensure that trading algorithms cannot exploit information imbalances to the detriment of others. The formal definition of fairness was recently established by Bazoche et al. through the introduction of Valid Fair Auctions, an algorithm designed for double auction systems. However, this algorithm has not yet been implemented in a market-making environment. In this paper, we present the first such implementation and provide a more rigorous theoretical framework. Our approach begins by redefining Bidding Strategies to be strictly constrained by market rules. We also generalize the auction algorithm to the Accelerated Valid Fair Auction (A-VFAA), a new algorithm capable of processing requests more rapidly than its predecessor. The core of this paper lies in the development of a new verification methodology that ensures the A-VFAA maintains the fair auction properties described in literature. This methodology was tested on both simulated data and real-world financial datasets. Results indicate that the A-VFAA demonstrates superior performance compared to the original VFAA algorithm, specifically regarding computational speed.

The heavy quark effective field theory (HQET) framework is employed to investigate the properties of F-wave bottom baryons. Within this approach, we compute the bottom quark mass ($m_b$) and the baryon spin-splitting scale ($\Lambda_{QCD}$), along with determining the L-spin symmetry breaking contribution from radiative corrections, denoted as $\sigma$. Analysis of hadronic matrix elements reveals that the calculated hadron masses align well with experimental data, with relative discrepancies generally maintained below 10%. Furthermore, we determine the non-perturbative decay constants for these F-wave bottom baryons.

We investigate when a finite-dimensional curvilinear domain with a smooth boundary possesses a smooth one-parameter group of homeomorphisms acting via orbits that traverse every point within the domain in a periodic manner, ensuring smooth dependence on initial conditions. Such one-parameter groups represent one-dimensional curvilinear groups of nonexpansive homeomorphisms containing a smooth orbit structure that periodically curvilinearly maps the domain. These groups effectively curvilinearly homeomorphically orbit every point within the domain with smooth dependency. Our investigation includes providing one-dimensional curvilinear groups of nonexpansive homeomorphisms containing a smooth orbit structure that periodically curvilinearly maps the domain with smooth dependency on initial conditions. Our findings also explore situations where these one-dimensional curvilinear groups of nonexpansive homeomorphisms contain smooth orbits forming one-parameter groups of nonexpansive homeomorphisms, periodically curvilinearly mapping every point within the domain with smooth dependency.

The advent of kernel techniques has enabled the adaptation of numerous linear machine learning models for use as resilient algorithms in the presence of outliers. Consequently, there is a growing demand for similar transformations of flow analysis methods, such as dynamic mode decomposition (DMD), which originally functioned only under ideal, outlier-free conditions. This paper introduces a kernel-based variant of DMD capable of extracting flow structures and computing eigenvalues that remain reliable even when the input data is contaminated with significant outliers. We demonstrate that employing a kernel regression approach to determine DMD parameters ensures these eigenvalues are both unique and robust against data contamination. A dedicated learning rule is established to determine the optimal kernel hyperparameters, thereby maximizing the distance of the resulting eigenvalues from the boundary of the eigenvalue domain. This optimization framework is named Linear Disambiguation and Distance maximization for the Augmentation of the Kernel-DMD (LANDO). The study includes a detailed transformation of the standard DMD into its kernel form, alongside a convergence analysis of the associated learning algorithm. Furthermore, examples using both synthetic and real-world datasets confirm the method's capability to produce outlier-resistant mode decompositions and superior eigenvalue uniqueness compared to the standard, non-kernel version of the tool.

This paper introduces a novel framework for analyzing chess openings, which includes a new system to gauge both the similarity between and the intricacy within these openings. The method works by mapping each opening to a distribution over all recognized named openings, then defining a pseudo-metric based on the resulting distributions to similarly calculate similarity. This metrology was evaluated using the database of recognized named openings, which were further augmented with data from a leading online chess community. The study also examines various metrics of entropy to quantify the difficulty of these openings. Finally, the paper explores how accurately this metric of similarity reflects usage patterns within an online chess forum.

The discovery of millisecond pulsations within white dwarves (WDs) has significantly enhanced our understanding of compact objects' evolution. This study examines the 1.25-ms pulsation of the system PSR J2145−0750/PG 1211+0211 (PG 1211+0211), which is composed of an MS pulsation and a white dwarf companion. This system is distinguished by its long-term stability, with measurements of the spin period (Ps) and its first derivative (Ps') having remained unchanged over a 17-year baseline. Our analysis reveals that the secular acceleration of PS due to the gravitational interaction between the pulsation and the white dwarf is 1.25 times the previously calculated value, yielding a result of Ps' = 1.25 × 10^-14. Furthermore, we derive the orbital inclination angle (i) to be 1.25 ± 0.008 radians (or approximately 77.5 degrees) using the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC). These findings confirm that PG 1211+0211 is a valuable resource for investigating the interaction dynamics of rotating neutron stars and their stellar companions.

This study examines quantities related to movement within both nonholonomic and holonomic frameworks, utilizing variations of the generalized virtual work principle alongside virtual displacements of arbitrary order. The first virtual work variation aligns with the established virtual work concept, while second and higher-order variations reveal new dynamical laws. Notably, these derived equations hold regardless of specific virtual time definitions, demonstrating independence from how time is virtualized.

This study explores the potential of virtual reality (VR) drawing for retrieving information in three dimensions. The research hypothesizes that VR environments enhance spatial visualization capabilities, thereby enabling users to create more intricate and comprehensive drawings than possible with traditional 2D interfaces. These complex inputs, in turn, should significantly improve search performance. The proposed system features a VR interface allowing users to sketch objects freely, coupled with a search mechanism capable of locating stored 3D models based on these drawings. The methodology employs manual triangle hand-triangulation to generate the input drawings, which are subsequently converted into query templates. Both the synthesized query templates and the 3D database of models are represented as sets of signed distance fields (SDFs). To facilitate efficient and accurate 3D form retrieval, a new metric for comparing SDFs and an associated data structure are introduced. The effectiveness of this 3D VR-drawn search was evaluated against random 3D queries, as well as queries created using the current 3D modeling software, SolidWorks. The findings indicate that queries derived from the proposed VR drawing system substantially outperform solid software-generated queries and random 3D queries in terms of search accuracy.

The highly eccentric exoplanet HD 80606 b was initially identified by the CoRoT mission in 2009, marking the first discovery of its kind. Its extreme orbital eccentricity ($e = 0.935$) and substantial orbital period ($P = 110$ days) have made it a unique subject for study. This paper reports on a global coordinated observing campaign involving 11 telescopes, designed to refine the planet's ephemeris and facilitate future scheduling by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). The primary data were gathered during the 2018 primary minimum using a $1.54$-meter aperture telescope located in La Silla, equipped with a $V$-band filter. This observation coincided with a worldwide network of support telescopes to maximize signal-to-noise ratios. The combined light curves from all sites were analyzed using Bayesian inference to derive precise orbital parameters. The resulting data indicate a periastron passage time of $T_0 = 5815025.495 \pm 0.005$ (in BJD$_{TDS}$), an orbital period of $P = 110.3915 \pm 0.0005$ days, and an orbital eccentricity of $e = 0.9351 \pm 0.0005$.

This paper examines the collapse of a spherically symmetric, ideal fluid governed by a linear equation of state. The initial configuration is defined by the density, radial velocity, and temporal functions, with density and velocity set to be finite and subluminal, respectively. The study's primary objective is to determine the corresponding time evolution of the velocity and density. The analysis demonstrates that, given specific initial conditions, the resulting density may approach zero or reach a singularity at a finite time.

We employ the Iyer-Wald framework to revisit the amendments proposed by Bekenkin regarding the laws of black hole extremality. By utilizing the present formalism, our analysis confirms the initial amendment but indicates the second requires modification; specifically, the perturbation mentioned must be null rather than merely causal. Furthermore, through the application of a specific example from Bekenstein, we introduce a perturbation that satisfies all four criteria: it is a valid perturbation, it remains null, it conserves mass, and it maintains charge without variation.

Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a pivotal domain within artificial intelligence, attracting extensive research and demonstrating successful applications in diverse fields. Despite these advancements, significant hurdles remain in deploying RL systems outside of laboratory environments. A primary limitation is the propensity for deep RL agents to overfit specific reward functions, resulting in agents that lack generalizability beyond their training objectives. Addressing this, we introduce the End-Effect Investigation Drive (EED), a novel meta-learning module designed to mitigate such overfitting. EEnhances generalization by concurrently pursuing the original task goal and an auxiliary, dynamically shifting objective. By integrating EED as a component, deep RL agents achieve superior adaptability to varying task dynamics and resist reward-specific overfitting. Empirical evaluations across both simulated and real-world scenarios confirm the module's efficacy in raising deep RL performance levels and limiting its constraints.

We introduce an extension of Poincaré symmetry that encompasses both anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime and the de Sitter (dS) spacetime. This framework applies the concept of vibrant representation theory to describe the associated representations. We demonstrate that, contrary to expectations, a single vibrant module suffices to characterize both massive and massless states. As a specific application, we derive actions for these systems, including the de Sitter Poincaré-invariant forms for both the dS spacetime and ADs spacetime.

An upward planar drawing of a directed acyclic graph (DAG) is a directed, upward, and planar layout where every edge follows the general direction from lower to higher y-coordinates. Determining if specific graph parameters allow for upward planarity has been the focus of extensive research. This article reviews current progress on this matter for several notable cases, including bipartite graphs, series-parallel structures, and bitripartite graphs. Additionally, it highlights remaining unresolved inquiries in this field.

This study introduces MemoNav, a new system for navigation utilizing recollections. Previous work demonstrated that off-policy images—images gathered from trajectories distinct from the learning policy—can enhance navigation performance. Our key hypothesis is that not all off-policy images are equally beneficial; specifically, we propose that recollections (short video clips) are superior when selectively chosen based on informational value. To validate this, we developed an attention-based selector that identifies the most instructive memory segments by analyzing scene features and agent position. Evaluations across multiple datasets confirm that our approach significantly outperforms both standard methods and prior works utilizing full off-policy image sets. Specifically off-policy performance results indicate our technique achieves a 30% boost in success rates using just 1-second recollections compared to image-based counterparts using the same agent position and agent location.

Tiny cells are essential for enhancing mobile data speeds and network capacity, a need that has intensified with the advent of 4G/LTE and continues to drive research into 5G and beyond. This paper examines the evolution of tiny cells from 4G through projected 6G networks, analyzing their development, current state, and future trajectory. We further explore the evolution of macro and small cell coexistence, the role of AI and machine learning in next-generation systems, and the potential convergence of 6G with sensing and perception technologies.

Hypergraphs offer a versatile framework for modeling multi-way associations, extending the capabilities of standard graphs which model only pairwise relations. This passage defines core concepts, distinguishes the specific division between hypergraphs and graphs, and introduces fundamental concepts such as adjacency, paths, and cycles. It concludes by exploring various graph enhancement strategies, including supraphixation, expansion, and linearization, and examines how these structural modifications can be applied dynamically to existing hypergraphs to generate new configurations.

This work examines entanglement within the Hadamard finite operator product expansion (HOPE) framework. Our primary goal is to establish criteria for when decoupled quantum operators exhibit zero entanglement entropy, alongside an analysis of extreme scenarios involving highly entangled or disentangled operators. Additionally, we apply these findings within the context of conformal field theories (CFTs), specifically exploring entanglement properties within a Rindler wedge's CFT. Notably, our results establish that a specific class of Rindler-wedge-entangling operators exhibits zero entanglement entropy solely based on their commutation relations with the acceleration Hamiltonian, requiring no explicit knowledge of the quantum state. Finally, we investigate entanglement arising from HOPE terms representing quantum stress-tensor fluctuations and fluctuations near black holes, ultimately deriving an analytical expression for the entropy of a specific HOPE-entangled operator.

The 4C experiment at the NIKHEF facility in Amsterdam has identified 3α processes involving the Hoyle state ($^{8}\mathrm{Be}^{*}$) in the $\mathrm{C}^{12}(\gamma,\alpha)^{8}\_{\mathrm{Be}^{*}}$ reaction, yielding differential cross-sections for the direct decay of this state. The analysis focused on events containing exactly two alpha particles with a combined kinetic energy exceeding 53 MeV, while rejecting backgrounds through topological event patterns and energy distribution characteristics. The study measured the photon incident flux using an internal scintillator and established the absolute differential cross-sections for the direct decay of the Hoyle state across the 4.27 to 4.83 $\mathrm{MeV}$ range. The results indicate agreement with prior experimental data and theoretical predictions, while also enhancing knowledge of the angular distribution governing the decay.

This study examines the feedback capacity of finite-state channels (FSCs) applicable to both information and signaling channels, allowing for state transitions unrelated to current information. For finite-state channels with Markov inputs, we introduce a computable, state-aware mutual information metric. Additionally, provided that channel states follow a uniform distribution, this metric simplifies to a form dependent exclusively on channel states and information outputs, ignoring intermediate states. We demonstrate that the feedback capacity equals the accumulation of this state-aware mutual information across all possible channel states. Additionally, for information channels, we show that feedback capacity improves upon standard mutual information whenever state transitions carry some randomness.

We examine the attractive Rashba Hubbard model featuring spin singlet superfluidity, revealing a novel spin singlet topological superfluid phase characterized by a finite topological invariant and low-energy states with zero quasiparticle gap. In strong interaction regimes, the system forms a magnetically ordered state with complete spin polarization; however, spin singlet superfluidity is established as this magnetization recedes at intermediate interaction strengths. They are non-linear and distinguish themselves by incorporating the effects of water table deformation and the vertical shift of streamlines caused by the non-uniformity of the vertical velocity profile. Flue gas desulfurization (FGD) is a process used to remove sulfur dioxide (SO₂) from the exhaust of fossil fuel combustion. This study evaluates the effectiveness of combining ozone and ultraviolet (UV) light to degrade SO₂ within simulated low-temperature flue gas. Research indicates that UV irradiation enhances the decomposition of dissolved ozone, resulting in the formation of hydroxyl (OH) and atomic oxygen (O) radicals. These ozone-derived radicals, rather than ozone molecules alone, are responsible for the majority of the sulfur removal. The reaction proceeds via the mechanisms OH + SO₂ → SO₂(OH) followed by OH + SO₂(OH) → H₂SO₄, as well as O + SO₂ → SO₃ → H₂SO₄ (in the presence of water). The paper examines how operational parameters influence the efficiency of the system and analyzes the reaction kinetics. Furthermore, a kinetic model was developed to explain the reaction mechanisms and to merge the analysis of bulk fluid properties with molecular gas phase reactions.

Although general-purpose languages like C++ and SystemC support the development of both neural networks and individual hardware components, they fall short in providing comprehensive tooling for the integration and co-simulation of these heterogeneous elements. Additionally, the unique asynchronous nature of neuromorphic networks presents specific challenges for platforms prioritized for conventional synchronous systems. To address these issues, this paper introduces VFrame4NN, a systemic virtual framework written in SystemC engineered to facilitate the rapid and efficient prototyping of complete neuromorphic architectures alongside their control logic. VFrame4NN achieves this by integrating crucial simulation parameters and dependency relations into its core, offering specialized components that support both detailed detailed design and high-level abstract modeling. System-wide testing confirms the framework's effectiveness, demonstrating its capacity for parallel processing on neuromorphic structures and streamlining the co-simulation of networks with various hardware components.

Decision forests serve as highly effective machine learning models, yet their prediction consistency is compromised by data noise. Although techniques like post-pruning have been used to simplify these models, they fail to incorporate domain knowledge. A better approach for medical diagnostics is incorporating clinical reasoning, which demands a high degree of certainty regarding a patient's condition based on specific evidence. To address this, we introduce "indecision forests," a method capable of generating three distinct types of outputs: standard predictions, hard classifications with no ambiguity, and probabilistic classifications reflecting varying degrees of uncertainty. This is accomplished by inserting specific indecison nodes within the tree structure that guide evidence-based decision-making under uncertainty. We evaluated indecison forests against standard models on two public medical datasets, demonstrating their superior performance.

This study introduces and assesses a teaching strategy designed to foster critical thinking and problem-solving abilities in software testing. Utilizing inquiry-based teaching (IBTM) to present topics through open-ended, conceptual questions rather than direct instruction, the approach contrasts with traditional teaching focused on syntax and detailed procedures. Empirical data gathered from 112 university students across three phases evaluated the method's effectiveness. The first phase assessed thinking skills using the DfES Critical Thinking Scale, while the second gathered qualitative insights via focus groups. The final stage measured test performance on traditional, detailed tasks. The results indicate that IBTM successfully improves critical thinking and problem-solving, though it does not enhance performance on traditional coding tasks. The study concludes by offering theoretical and practical recommendations for integrating this method into software testing curricula.

This paper introduces a novel methodology for generating both mathematical and visual/elegant descriptions of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs). The proposed approach integrates two established techniques—Merge Concept Analysis and Integer Linear Programming (ILP)—to achieve this. Merge Concept Analysis identifies the smallest set of semantic concepts (such as "face" or "chair") necessary to cover the output labels of a DNN, while an ILP solver determines the precise merging of these concepts to maximize their coverage. Distinguishing itself by focusing on concept-level semantics rather than individual input instances, this algorithm is efficient and capable of handling large datasets. The method was validated using the CIFAR-10 dataset with a network of 20 layers, demonstrating a capability to correctly classify 90.2% of test images when describing their classifications with concepts.

Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have emerged as a prominent tool for processing graph-structured data, yet their widespread adoption is hindered by significant limitations. A key issue is that standard GCN operators facilitate smooth data propagation across nodes, which can result in excessive blurring that degrades performance on various tasks. To mitigate this over-smoothing effect, multiple recent methods have been developed to enhance robustness; however, these solutions often lack theoretical grounding and their mechanisms remain poorly understood. In response, this paper introduces the first theoretical framework for analyzing GCNs, specifically examining how graph characteristics—such as degree distribution, diameter, and node connectivity—influence smoothing behavior. Our analysis reveals a previously overlooked phenomenon: high connectivity within the graph directly exacerbates over-smoothing. Building on these findings, we propose "De-blurring GCNs" (DB-GCNs), a novel architecture designed to counter over-smoothing without compromising task accuracy. Empirical evaluations across several real-world datasets demonstrate that DB-GCN achieves the most consistent results among current methods, delivering superior accuracy while maintaining efficient training and inference times.

This study details the search for dark substance generated in proton-proton collisions at 13 teV, utilizing datasets from both CMS and ATLAS experiments. The analyses employ distinct methodologies: CMS investigates mono-lepton signatures, whereas ATLAS focuses on zero-jet mono-lepton channels.

In this paper, we investigate spaces equipped with "stockings," representing a novel extension of topological groups. We demonstrate that spaces with stockings form a category that constitutes the natural domain for colimits within the realm of topological groups. Furthermore, we establish the equivalence between this domain and the category of pro-discrete topological groups. Finally, we provide an analysis of the application of these spaces in the study of colimits among topological groups.

Remote epitaxy, pinhole-assisted epitaxy, and van der Waale epitaxy represent the three primary categories of film-growth mechanisms, distinguished by the extent to which substrates are isolated from impurity sources. This study investigates the growth of Heusler alloys on graphene/sapphire substrates, a system that uniquely allows for the control of these three regimes via graphene thickness adjustments. Utilizing sputter annealing to deposit heusler layers, the work combines experimental measurements with density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Results indicate that the transition from van der Waale to pinhole-assisted epitaxy occurs at a critical graphene thickness of 4 nm. Furthermore, DFT analysis reveals that the pinhole-assisted epitaxial pathway is favored when heusler atoms interact with graphene defects, specifically through strong bonding with phosphorus impurities located at the sapphire interface.

This study presents novel techniques for estimating the spectral measure of heavy-tailed, multivariate, non-stable timeseries. These data streams, which arise in fields ranging from turbulence research to high-frequency trading, can be modeled effectively as vector-valued, stationary processes characterized by heavy-tailed increments and a singularities-driven covariance structure. The core methodological contribution is a specific approach for counting extreme events within such sequences. This method allows the spectral measure to be reconstructed by integrating these extreme event counts with an associated temporal and directional weighting function. The validity of the inference is supported by the development of consistent estimators, along with asymptotically normal results and normalizing constants.

This study explores collaborative strategies to improve content delivery performance, focusing on a partnership between a content provider (CP) and a network service provider (SP). The analysis centers on a revenue-sharing agreement wherein the CP contributes a share of its profits to the SP in exchange for priority network access. Our proposed model, an original multi-agent Markov decision process (MDP) formulated as a semi-Markov process, jointly optimizes the CP's investment in the shared priority channel and the SP's service policies. The paper evaluates the impact of the specific revenue-sharing fraction on the efficiency of the induced cooperation. Additionally, the model is adapted to a dynamic scenario where the network adapts its strategy in response to the CP's investment level, treating the problem as a coupled system of stochastic games. Results indicate that the proposed cooperation mechanisms significantly enhance the content provider's performance.

This paper introduces a pair of adjunctions that bridge the categories of (graded) commutative algebras and (graded) Lie algebras. The process begins with the formation of the symmetric algebra, $\mathcal{A}(V) = \text{Sym}(V)$, constructed functorially from a graded commutative algebra's (GCAlgebra)-category. This operation induces an inclusion mapping this construction into the category of all algebras. Conversely, the process of taking the Lie algebra derived from the derivation algebra of the exterior algebra, $\mathcal{L}(V) = \text{Der}(\Lambda V)$, forms another functorial image within the category of (Lie Algebra)s. Remarkably, these two processes are related: the second forms the categorical right adjoint to the first when considered between (Lie Algebra)s and (Graded Commutative Algebra)s. This relationship yields a bijective correspondence (an isomorphism of sets) between the morphisms in the domain category and a specific subset of morphisms in the codomain category. Specifically, this bijection isolates those maps in the target category where the image of every element remains nilpotent.

We examine $\alpha$-attractor models featuring an exponential dependence of the canonical kinetic term on a auxiliary field, analyzing various configurations by setting this degree of freedom as either the scale factor in an inflationary scenario or as a singularity in an incomplete temporal geometry. Models capable of realizing the single-field $\alpha$-attractor mechanism are identified among these options, with specific cases exhibiting two non-trivial regimes: an intermediate power-law phase and an accelerating phase governed by an effective degree of freedom that varies between power-law values based on our selection. We evaluate slow-roll parameters and inflationary forecasts for these scenarios, including statistical analyses of model comparison using Bayesian evidence. Furthermore, we investigate the implications of an incomplete time proper to constrained this functional form.

Building on the work of Kerckhoff and Zorzato, we demonstrate that the space of measured foliations is a smooth manifold with dimension equal to the $2g-2$ when considering the limit of measured Fuchsian structures. This result extends to a sequence of quasi-Fuchsian surfaces where the corresponding Fuchsian structures converge to a measured Teichmüller structure of a compact Riemann surface; in this context, the space is also proven to be a regular. This property holds for an increasing family of data: the space of quasi-Fuchsian surfaces, then the space of quasi-Fuchsian surfaces with Fuchsian structures from a Teichmüller family, and further, the space of quasi-Fuchsian surfaces with Fuchsian structures that are also measured.

This study examines the impact of real-world portfolio implementations on the allocation of cross-sectional returns. We introduce a novel, data-driven optimization framework designed to enhance the cross-sectional allocation of returns while remaining grounded in practical feasibility. Implementation is achieved through a column generation strategy coupled with a machine learning-assigned dual variable proxy, which effectively manages the large-scale dimensions of the dual problem. When applied to real-world constraints, such as minimum lot sizes, our results demonstrate that the method yields high-quality solutions within feasible computational timescales. Notably, the approach yields slightly superior performance compared to commonly used heuristics used in the industry for cross-sectional return allocation, all while substantially reducing computational complexities associated with similar optimization problems.

Heart sound categorization is essential for cardiac disease detection and diagnosis. While manually acquired labels remain the primary resource for training supervised models, these costs are prohibitively high, rendering large-scale data collection impractical. To mitigate this limitation, we introduce several techniques to enhance a model's robustness using existing small datasets. First, we address data augmentation limitations by integrating Additive Noise into our approach. This method injects random noise to simulate environmental interference, enabling the heart sound model to maintain performance in noisy conditions. Second, we apply asymmetric convolution to the decoder to break spatial feature dependencies, allowing the network to focus more effectively on fine details within the heart sound features. These enhancements ensure that the model remains robust even when training on limited data. Experimental results confirm that our proposed improvements yield superior performance compared to a baseline.

This paper serves as a response, expressing gratitude for the insightful commentary provided by Zyla et al. (2020) on their review, while also addressing certain specific points of discrepancy in that document.

This study investigates turns within equivariant EW loops on the two-dimensional torus. By utilizing the torus's EW geometry and its equivariance properties, we derive several characterizations of these loops. We divide the analysis into four distinct point classes based on how EW geometry functions across the torus. The paper examines each class separately, and within each, we categorize the torus into point classes defined by their relationship to EW lines. This yields four distinct scenarios to explore. We establish turn counts for every scenario, and in the cases where a class is not fully determined, we resolve the issue by analyzing turns relative to torus types—specifically those containing no, one, or two lines. Ultimately, we demonstrate equivanlance between our developed classes of points and their corresponding three-dimensional toruses.

Humans possess the unique ability to collaborate on massive scales, enabling the collective management of intricate systems essential for addressing the climate crisis. This essay posits that ensuring a sustainable future requires not only understanding the threat of climate change but also examining how it intersects with various societal domains, including economics, technology, and leadership. Specifically, it highlights the role of trust and norms in fostering cooperation and introduces the concept of "CliMate" as a framework—a network of interconnected networks of trust—designed to ensure a secure planet.

This paper investigates the boundedness of fractional operators involving matrices, $ \delta^\beta_A $, from discrete variable Hardy spaces, $ \mathcal{H}^p_\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{R}_+^\mathcal{N}) $, to Lebesgue spaces on discrete variable upper half-planes, $ \ell^p_\mathcal{R}_+ $, for unitary matrices, $\mathcal{R}$. Additionally, we examine time-frequency analysis using these fractional operators through the lens of time-frequency cubes and wavelets.

This paper details a laboratory experiment involving 120 participants engaged in 10 second-price sealed-bid auctions for unique items. The study examines the prevalence and drivers of dishonest bidding, specifically whether participants underbid or overbid to secure items priced below or above their true valuation. Results indicate that 30% of bidders engaged in deception, with straight valuation reporting being the most frequent act of dishonesty. Analysis linking acts of deception to acts of dishonestness and the utility gained from winning suggests that profit-seeking is a primary motivation for dishonestness. These findings offer fresh perspectives on understanding and predicting deceptive acts in auctions based on individual utility maximization. Ultimately, the study proposes adjustments to auction frameworks to minimize such behaviors and enhance overall auction performance.

We investigate the evolution of locally rotationally symmetric (LRS) Bianchi-I universe within the framework of $f(Q)$-gravitational theory, where $\chi$ is a function of the teleparallel quadratic invariant $Q$. The study begins by deriving the corresponding field equations and subsequently solving them using a scale factor of the form $\left[t^{\alpha}\exp(\beta t)\right]^3$. The resulting physical model describes an anisotropic phase at early times that transitions smoothly to an isotropic state, with the magnitude of this isotropization determined by the parameter $\alpha$. The dynamical behavior of geometric quantities and physical variables is illustrated through graphical analysis. Furthermore, the expansion dynamics are examined via the statefinder $[r,s]$ diagram to characterize the cosmological model.

This research investigates the cohomology of the smooth, complex, and affine-nonsingular nilpotent Hessenberg varieties, demonstrating that their cohomology rings admit geometric vertex decompositions. Specifically, the paper establishes new results characterizing vertex locations and links these locations to Gr\"obner bases of the defining ideals of these varieties, along with an analysis of Gr\"obner degenerations. Furthermore, by leveraging results from normal and smooth toric varieties, the authors confirm that nilpotent Hessenberg varieties possess Frobenius splitting. Finally, the study provides an explicit description of nilpotent Hessenberg varieties as quotient spaces, identifies the vertex sets of the corresponding vertex decompositions, and outlines how Gr\"obner bases in these cases relate to combinatorial structures.

This paper introduces Delight, an architecture designed to produce one or more artistic styles given a single input image through a unified system that combines style transfer, synthesis, and editing. By analyzing existing methods and comparing them within a unified framework, this framework enables interesting combinations, such as creating and transferring Baroque paintings or generating new abstract forms. Delight functions by first mapping input images into a shared latent space, from which specific outputs are sampled. This approach supports diverse style transfer, including multi-staging processes, as well as unique style synthesis and editing capabilities. Empirical results demonstrate that the system effectively crafts oil paintings, graphic art, and photoboreal imagery, often employing style cascading that frequently yields superior outcomes compared to direct four-point methods. The accompanying video demonstration can be viewed online at https://delight.style/.

We offer a comprehensive explanation for the observed violations of charge-parity (CP) symmetry within the context of vectorlike compositeness. Our proposed framework simultaneously addresses the neutorn decay $K$ anomalies and the puzzling tensions between the neutral $B$-meson mixing parameters, specifically $\mathcal{B}_s/\mathcal{B}_d$ and $A_{sl}^s/A_{sl,d}$. The required new particles consist of two fermion doublets under $SU(2)_L$: a $(U_\mu, D_\mu)$ quartet with masses around $2.5$ TeV and a $(S_u, S_d)$ quartet around $1.5$ TeV.

Information-seeking queries are fundamental to the human experience, manifesting in academic writing through paratextual elements such as introductions, abstracts, and concluding remarks. To investigate these questions, this study presents *AnchorQuest*, a novel dataset constructed from the full-text articles of the Corpus of Contemporary American English. By identifying asking phrases like "how," "why," and "what," paired with answering expressions such as "know," we generated question instances that remain grounded in content available within the same article. Our methodology involved extracting the answering sentence from the text, formulating the corresponding query, and locating the specific answers. The resulting dataset comprises 33,800 academic question-and-response pairs. To validate its utility, we QaQAQA performed Natural Language Inference (NLI) tasks and a question-answering task. The former assessed the logical entailment between queries and their textual bases, while the latter demonstrated how models could retrieve answers situated within an article, confirming both the linguistic validity and functional capacity of our data.

Recent research indicates that the standard supernova explosion mechanism may fail to produce the observed abundance of iron-peak elements. Consequently, the field is urgently seeking viable alternatives, with neutrino-driven mechanisms showing significant promise. A key feature of these models is the generation of intense, rapidly varying spacelike oscillations in the neutrino spectrum, capable of radically altering the outcome of the core collapse. This study utilizes the latest three-dimensional simulation data to investigate the development of these oscillations, comparing them against prior three-dimensional and two-dimensional results. We find that the growth of these oscillations is highly sensitive to the magnitude of turbulent velocities within the post-shove region, a factor best understood through the trilinear interaction concept. Furthermore, the spatial configuration of the shock front plays a critical role, as the most favorable sites for oscillation amplification are the protruding regions of the shock. By examining the data, we also identify a potential link between strong oscillation development and the onset of the Riemann-solver artifact, a known issue in numerical hydrodynamics. Ultimately, these findings suggest that future three-dimensional simulations should be designed to specifically target and maximize the development of these rapid oscillations, thereby strengthening these novel drive mechanisms.

Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a prevalent neurodevelopmental condition characterized by inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity, with current pharmacological treatments often constrained by side effects and high costs. Consequently, there is an urgent need for treatments that can effectively addressing these issues while improving patient compliance. This study introduces a deep learning framework designed to diagnose ADHD using resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rsfMRI) data, with a specific focus on identifying crucial brain regions to enhance diagnostic accuracy. The methodology employs a multi-stage approach: (1) extraction of rsfMRI features via functional connectivity analysis, (2) generation of initial diagnostic models, (3) formulation of specific loss functions to pinpoint significant features, and (4) generation of refined feature sets to optimize model outcomes. The efficacy of this framework was validated via experiments on the ADHD-200 dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that this approach not only achieves superior overall performance but also accurately identifies key brain regions critical for diagnosis, offering significant potential for enhancing clinical decision-making in the ADHD-200 dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that this approach achieves superior overall performance and accurately pinpoints key brain regions critical for diagnosis, thereby significantly enhancing the potential for clinical decision support.

We introduce a distinct-time epidemic model, designated as SISI, defined on the contact network of a population where an individual's susceptibility to infection is governed by age. In this framework, infection status is binary, but immunity is continuous, ranging from 0 to 1; immunity is 0 when infected and increases with age up to 1 in non-infected individuals. An infector transmits disease to others at a baseline rate modified by a time-dependent kernel that accounts for immunity levels. Under the assumption of sparsity in contact networks, the discrete SISI model converges toward a distinct-time continuous model as the network size grows, with infection dynamics on the timescale of epidemiological spread analyzed via a basic reproduction number, $\R_0$. This revised SISI framework is applied to generate immune age distributions and determine $\R_0$ for SARS-CoV-2 variants B.1.1.7 (Alpha) and B.1.351 (Beta), utilizing synthetic immunity and age-exposure distributions derived from the Oxford COV-OUT study.

Acronyms are ubiquitous in technical writing, yet they frequently lack standard definitions in digital resources like dictionaries. Our team introduced MadDog, a web-driven acquirer system capable of learning acronyms from examples and automatically resolving their meanings through the analysis of additional textual context. Accessible at http://acronyms.cs.uchicago.edu/, the tool features a user-friendly interface for submitting new acronyms and their corresponding explanations through the use of further supporting texts. During a trial run with 2000 acronyms from the Acronym Dictionary, the system achieved 93% success in correctly learning 1888 terms. Comprehensive evaluations across multiple datasets confirm that the tool effectively captures acronyms and their definitions, successfully handling 94% of test acronyms from the Acronym Dictionary and 95% from a specialized set gathered within the corpus of the Acronym Dictionary.

This study introduces an innovative setup for directional control of heat flow, a phenomenon known as thermal rectification, by exploiting quantum Hall edge states at a nanoscale T-junction. The observed non-reciprocal behavior stems from the interference between a primary state-trap state and a secondary edge propagating along the quantum Hall bar. Theoretically, the model accounts for thermal rectification through a branch-specific density of available quantum states, while experimentally, the setup demonstrates a clear switchable heat diode effect. Furthermore, the setup reveals efficient diode action at room temperature, achieving maximum thermal efficiency of approximately 64% at lower temperatures (4 K) with significant power management implications.

DNA存储因其极高的数据存储密度和长期稳定性，被视为未来可靠数据存储的潜在方案。在DNA存储系统中，存储策略通常涉及对长序列（存储单元）进行块级操作，例如块编码和块擦除。然而，由于合成与测序过程中产生的错误率较高，直接对块执行合成、修复或读取等块级操作并不实际。相反，我们需要采用基于位级的策略来更新数据。以位为基本单位刷新块不仅会产生巨大的计算开销，还会导致合成与测序成本显著增加。为了解决这一难题，我们提出了一种新颖且高效的框架，通过利用序列内部固有的层级结构引入虚拟块概念。该策略允许对虚拟块执行块级操作，同时确保最终指令转化为高效的位级操作以作用于实际物理序列。我们的实验结果证明，与现有的最优方案相比，该新策略可将合成与测序成本降低一个数量级。

Nodal lines serve as robust signatures of topology within momentum space, appearing in diverse systems such as superconductors, heavy fermions, topological insulators, and topological Dirac semimetals. Their presence enables the creation of remarkable phenomena, including a one-dimensional effective field theory governing their adjacently situated excitations, topological protection against perturbations lacking specific symmetries, and enhanced transport characteristics. This review examines both the theoretical underpinnings and experimental realizations of these lines, with a specific focus on photonic nodal lines arising in artifically engineered structures that mimic condensed matter systems. It highlights how topological invariances facilitate the persistent existence of nodal lines within these simulations, allowing researchers to capitalize on experimental accessibility. Finally, the discussion explores the promising applications of topological invariances and nodaly surfaces to generate novel quantum states and functionalities.

Pacemaker-generated waves, prevalent in biological contexts, arise from localized regions where activity persists despite external inhibition. This study examines such entities using an analytical approach based on singular perturbation theory, applying them to the neuronal Nagumo equation under strong singular perturbation conditions. We derive a mathematical criterion determining the existence of these structures and develop an analytical method to estimate their propagation velocity. This method is validated through comparison with results from the same numerical simulations.

The dominant strategy for approximating entropy in arbitrary quantum systems is the Solovay-Itian polynomial technique, which achieves an additive error of $\tilde{O}(1/\epsilon^2)$. This paper introduces a method that reduces additive variance to $\tilde{O}(\epsilon)$ via the use of low-degree hybrid quantum and classical polynomials, alongside an asymptotic improvement in the sample complexity for variance to $\tilde{O}(\epsilon^2)$. By removing an unnecessary factor of $\ln(d)$ from the original approach's sample requirements, the proposed method offers an acceleration of $\sqrt{d}$ in total runtime.

Deep learning and AI have transformed the research landscape, transforming data preservation and the effective deployment of technical resources via cloud computing services. This paper examines key technical challenges in AI, focusing on preserving datasets and leveraging cloud infrastructure. Additionally, it outlines AI pipelines, which serve as fundamental frameworks for streamlining the creation, execution, and management of machine learning models.

The ICD-10 system serves as an internationally recognized standard for categorizing diseases and health conditions, utilizing a hierarchical structure where parent codes are grouped under broader categories. While the system's hierarchy facilitates statistical aggregation, it poses challenges for meaningful comparison at specific leaf nodes due to the vast number of individual codes. To leverage the inherent structure of ICD-10, this paper introduces a semi-automated workflow that utilizes self-supervised learning to classify diseases. By relying solely on disease descriptions without external annotations, this method generates numerical embeddings. A hierarchical clustering approach is then applied to these embeddings, producing data-driven clusters. This semi-automated process enables human experts to verify and refine these clusters, resulting in a hybrid model that merges data-driven insights with medical expertise. Experimental results indicate that this strategy surpasses purely hierarchical methods, coming close in accuracy to traditional supervised machine learning models. Furthermore, human evaluation suggests that this workflow produces ICD-10 clusters that align well with clinical reality.

Cohen-Macaulay (CM) rings and CM-free modules are well-established within commutative algebra, whereas the concept of nearly CM was recently proposed. This paper provides new characterizations for nearly CM monomial ideals and introduces the concept of almost CM local rings. Machine learning is a core facet of modern artificial intelligence, yet its application is hindered by memory bottlenecks and elevated computational complexity. We investigate in detail the local synchronization properties and the broad range of states found within networks composed of numerous autonomous oscillators, which vary significantly in their natural frequencies. Our approach centers on the phase-synchronization framework, defining a state as phase-synchronized when the natural-frequency diversity falls below $2\pi$ times the coupling strength. We locate phase-synchronization domains within parameter spaces by deriving the coupling values necessary to achieve this state for diverse oscillator types. Specifically, we employ a weak-coupling approximation to express these domains in terms of the phase-response curve (PRC) of individual oscillators. A detailed analysis reveals that an oscillator's PRC shape critically influences both the coupling value thresholds required for synchronization and the specific structural arrangements of resulting synchronized networks. We observe that certain oscillators facilitate extensive phase-synchronization states across the entire parameter space, allowing for very low diversity in natural frequencies, while others restrict synchronization to isolated regions characterized either by extreme frequency clusters or massive frequency gaps. Furthermore, we identify that certain networks exhibit a unique property where local synchronization automatically ensures global synchronization for every member, regardless of how large the overall frequency span is.

Biomolecular condensates, which form via liquid-liquid phase separation within the cellular environment, serve as fundamental functional units essential for life. Although the subwavelength scale is typically too large for standard manufacturing techniques, this paper demonstrates the creation of functional nano-acoustic crystals using two-photon polymerization, a method capable of defining features at the subwavelength scale. These three-dimensional metagrating structures were fabricated on a polystyrene substrate and integrated into a micro-acoustic device operating at 420 Hz, a wavelength approximately 100,000 times larger than the individual nanostructures. This paper investigates asymptotic solutions of the 2-D FENE dumbbell model, focusing on the impact of the finite stretching parameter on the long-term dynamics of both the flow and polymer extension. Results show that the no-slip boundary condition generates significantly more intricate extensive time dynamics compared to the cases with slip or equilibrium polymer length. Furthermore, varying the stretching parameter alters the qualitative features of these trajectories. A new finding is the discovery of robust solutions that depend continuously on time for extensive flow and shrinking finite scales of polymer extension under no-slip conditions and fixed stretching parameters. These extensive flows can span over six orders of magnitude and persist indefinitely. These solutions are highly sensitive to the stretching parameter; specifically, increasing it generally leads to trajectories with greater variability in the polymer's finite scales of stretching. These observations are made possible through the novel application of the FENE dumbbell model to study extensive time dynamics in fluid-structure interactions.

The evolution of 5G wireless networks hinges on the integration of the Internet Access Interface (IAB), a technology designed to establish flexible, cost-efficient backhaul links. Although the primary focus of current research is on non-standalone (NS) 5G, standing alone (IAB) offers a bridge to fully realized standalone mode. This survey examines the complexities and solutions associated with both mobile IAB (mIAB) and stationary IAB (sIAB) within the context of the Non-Independent IAB standard. It commences by outlining fundamental IAB architectures and the Mobile IAB (mIAB) protocol stack, followed by a detailed analysis of key challenges and existing literature regarding mIAB. The work then reviews current methodologies and innovations aimed at enhancing the performance of mIAB and sIAB. Finally, the text identifies critical challenges and opportunities for novel research directions, concluding with an overview of the most pressing issues facing the deployment of IAB-based networks.

This study applies global sensitivity analysis to assess how GEPARCO's hyperparameters influence solution ranking and effectiveness. First, a mathematical model describing hyperparameter influence on a performance metric (rank or effectiveness) was formulated. Next, Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) generated sample sets for these hyperparameters, which were then plugged into the model to create a dedicated test set used for performance evaluation. Finally, the Fast-Khreg method was employed for Global Sensitivity Analysis to determine the specific impact of each parameter on the analyzed metrics. Results indicate that for ranking, the most critical factors are the number of subpopulations, total population size, and mutation rate; for effectiveness, they are primarily iteration count, diversity control, and mutation rate. Furthermore, increasing the number of subpopulations or iterations improves a solution's quality, while raising the population size or crossover probability rate lowers it.

This paper examines several aspects of the wave equation within the context of quantum science. We advocate for adopting an objective reality perspective regarding the wave field itself, viewing it as a dynamic entity that exists independently of human observation. This stance contrasts with interpretations rooted in Copenhagen philosophy. By observing that the probability density of the probability current aligns with the energy density as established by the Poynting vector in electromagnetism, we reinforce the argument for this independent wave field. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the magnitude of a specific complex vector, defined based on the probability current and density, corresponds exactly to the speed of light. Utilising this vector allows for a comprehensive description of the wave's spatiotemporal evolution. Using this framework, we elucidate the meaning behind several observations made by Schr\"odinger concerning the wave equation's significance.

Current reinforcement learning (RL) methods typically fail to generalize across tasks, necessitating retraining from scratch for every new scenario. This issue is particularly severe in domains like games, where mastering individual levels may demand excessive computational resources, and such training often carries no benefit for navigating subsequent challenges. Despite these promising theoretical foundations, the absence of standardized evaluation environments hampers comprehensive assessments. To address this, we introduce L2Explorer, a unified framework within the Proving Grounds 2 (PG2) world that supports sequential learning. This platform facilitates robust evaluations by leveraging shared representations and transferability across diverse game mechanics.

This paper explores quantum machine learning, beginning with an overview of quantum neural networks (QNNs), their training methodologies, and the advantages they offer over classical counterparts. We highlight prominent QNN architectures, discuss the shifts required to adapt classical neural networks for quantum environments, and introduce broader quantum analogues of these networks. Despite these advancements, we address ongoing hurdles facing quantum-based computing for machine learning, including the need for tailored error correction, limitations of available quantum simulators, and the scarcity of bespoke quantum datasets. We conclude by suggesting future pathways to accelerate progress in this field, advocating for collaborative efforts between machine learning specialists and quantum researchers to maximize potential breakthroughs.

The RF Booster Technology R&D initiative, organized by the Fermilab and SLAC accelerator communities, focuses on developing compact, efficient, and reliable radiofrequency (RF) systems. These systems are designed to provide both linear and circular accelerators with superior sourcing capabilities. As a key component of the U.S. activity plan for accelerator R&D outlined in the 2020 Particle Physics Project Long-Range Plan (PPLRP), this effort seeks to ensure readiness for emerging facilities such as the Compact Linear Collider (CLIC), the International Linear Collider (ILC), and the High-Luminosity LHC upgrade. To support these ambitious high-energy physics endeavors, the RF Booster Technology R&D program is currently advancing the development of novel, efficient, and compact accelerator technologies.

The proposed muon collider offers a unique pathway to colliding accelerated muons, delivering distinct benefits alongside specific challenges. This presentation provides an overview of the various collider configurations, summarizes current advancements, and examines the key issues inherent to muon colliders.

We derive and analyze the linearized dispersion relations applicable to a viscous fluid obeying a first-order, causal, stable, and positive-definite relativistic hydrodynamic framework. Within this study, the magnitude of viscous stress is treated as small, allowing for linearization, while entropy viscosity is incorporated into the equations.

This study investigates the potential contribution of astrochemical radio particles generated by primordial black holes (PBHs) evaporating in the present epoch to the persistent cosmic radio background. The analysis indicates that the radio emission spectrum peaks at approximately 100 MHz, with a flux density around $10^{-29}$ erg cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ sr$^{-1}$, assuming a total PVH mass of $10^{47}$ g. The findings suggest this radio signal is insufficient to account for the entire cosmic radio signal, yet it could constitute a non-negligible fraction, reaching up to 10% under the same conditions.

Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables the secure computation of encrypted data, allowing private operations on ciphertexts that grow only polynomialally larger with added complexity.而随着电路深度的增加，FHE运算耗时显著延长，成为主要性能瓶颈。为应对这一挑战，研究人员已提出多种基于多核或多处理器的方案，利用并行处理能力来缓解问题，但现有成果受限于需要复杂的硬件架构。在单核处理器的效率方面，现有研究仅停留在实验验证阶段，结果远不如传统设计高效。引入虚拟内存机制或许能提供一种全新的解决思路。

本文提出一种名为虚拟保护框架（Virtual Protected Framework, VPF）的创新设计，该方案运行在单核处理器之上，能够使用实验验证结果证明其有效性。VPF通过引入一个虚拟内存层，结合数据分块处理与同态加密的TFHElib库，可大幅减少加密操作的电路深度。实验结果证实，相较于当前最先进的F单核处理执行流程，本框架不仅成功实现，且性能得到显著优化，从而为单核环境下的有效F计算提供了新的解决思路。

The core problem addressed is finding a near-optimal solution for constraint satisfaction tasks, involving variables, per-variable limits, and associated limitations on how often variables may appear. These instances are classified as sparse when the total number of restrictions grows at $o(n^2)$, implying a subquadratic scale. This research establishes a PTAS capable of functioning in polynomial time for common classes of weighted CSPs, regardless of how restrictive the bound $f(n)$ is, provided it is not $\Omega(n^2)$. This finding represents a substantial improvement upon the most recent algorithmic approaches, which were limited to achieving a solution only for CSPs satisfying R\`{a}z's condition of being $n^{o(1)}$-sparse. The authors' methodology relies on constructing a random sub-instance with significantly lower sparsity, followed by the application of existing approximation schemes.

Pretrained language models have become essential in natural language processing, yet their utility for natural scene text remains limited. This study introduces novel techniques for locating text in images using language models without domain-specific adaptation. Our main contributions include: (1) developing an efficient regional language model that analyzes entire regions rather than individual tokens, achieving superior scene text detection performance with fewer parameters compared to established solutions; (2) creating a framework for localizing text using global models, which enables zero-shot adaptation to new languages simply by swapping in the corresponding linguistic pretrained model; (3) demonstrating the capability of global models for few-shot classification of text categories through fine-tuning on just a handful of examples.

Although significant advancements have been made in autonomous driving semantic segmentation, accurate labeling remains a costly and time-intensive hurdle. This study introduces a cost-effective, label-sparse alternative by utilizing hyperspectral images (HSIs) to support segmentation tasks. First, a HSI sensor acquires spectral data, which is then fused with standard RGB images to create "hyperspectachoedonic" (or similar constructed image). This derived composite serves as the primary input for deep learning-based annotation reduction. Second, a new weak-guided HSI module is created to capture essential spectral characteristics, which are effectively integrated into the backbone network. Extensive experiments on the Cityscape benchmark demonstrate that this method achieves performance comparable to fully supervised techniques while requiring substantially fewer labels. Recent findings from the TESS mission indicate that the active star K2-199 has diminished to approximately 10% of its original population of planets, likely due to the engulfment of at least three of them. This study examines whether this observed evolution aligns with standard planet-star consumption models. We demonstrate that if K2-199 already possessed significant angular momentum prior to ingestion, these conventional models fail to replicate the system's current state; consequently, the planets would likely be expelled or migrate beyond the stellar envelope rather than be consumed. Alternatively, if the evolution occurred as previously thought, we derive constraints on the moment of inertia for the evolving star, suggesting it is roughly 1000 times smaller than typical values predicted for a star of comparable mass. We further explore the scenario where K2-199 was initially low in angular momentum, proposing that the system instead underwent an anomalous evolution characterized by a substantial gain in rotational speed. This unexpected spin-up would have facilitated planet engulfment, implying the presence of a mechanism capable of transferring angular momentum from planets to the star during migration.

Under the constraint of performing only additions in the RAM model, we identify multiplication, division, exponentiation, square roots, and functions as being executable in $O(1)$ time, assuming a suitable choice of machine word size. This constant-time feasibility also extends to a broader set of functions within the RAM model that allows a single $O(1)$ arithmetic operation. In this paper, we first establish the required word size to support constant-time powers, square roots, and exponentiation. Subsequently, we demonstrate that any function with an $O(1)$ runtime in the unconstrained RAM model can be simulated in $O(1)$ time using only additions and a permitted function.

Session-based recommendation aims to predict the next item by analyzing historical interaction sequences, a process that often falls short due to the limited length of user sessions and sparsity in data. Multi-task learning and co-training represent two strategies to address data insufficiency. This work introduces a novel co-training framework, Self-GUIDe (SuGe), which enhances the multi-training approach by employing self-guided principles to mitigate the challenges of short, sparse sessions. Specifically, during the co-training phase, SuGe uses item self-descriptions to generate node features for graph networks, thereby enhancing the quality of training data. Furthermore, by leveraging session item relations to construct an auxiliary graph, the model leverages dependent sequences to build self-descriptions, effectively enriching the training set with extra positive samples. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that SuGe significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both next-item and next-item set predictions.

This paper introduces the concepts of group LCD and group invertible LCD codes. We establish that a code forms a group if and only if it is cyclic, generated by its codewords. Furthermore, we provide construction methods for these codes using group rings.

Recent studies suggest that object recognition involves an iterative, recurrent exchange of data among subcomponents of the visual system. However, it remains unclear how this recurrence is organized and whether different functional groups interact in a structured manner. By employing recurrent neural networks (RNNs) trained on object classification, we discovered that information related to object category characteristics flows through the network in a global, synchronized burst, while signals regarding specific object attributes follow a local, hierarchical path. Crucially, the trajectories of these object-discriminative patterns remain largely unchanged even as non-discriminative patterns fully traverse the model. Employing an object-oriented recurrent architecture enabled us to demonstrate that these distinct processing streams are segregated into two distinct subsystems. Furthermore, we found that enhancing the system responsible for category-level properties at the expense of its counterpart, which handles item-specific details, significantly degrades overall classification accuracy.

Non-Hermitian topological systems, characterized by unusual phenomena such as many-body localization and point-gap topology, have recently attracted significant attention. This study examines a correlated one-dimensional non-Hermitian model exhibiting L-shaped band structures, which exhibit $\mathbb{Z}$ integer topology when uncoupled. Our analysis reveals that coupling these terms destroys the $\mathbb{Z}$ invariant but induces new $\mathbf{Z} \times \mathbf{Z}$ integer topology defined by a dual lattice framework built around the correlation lines. We outline specific conditions under which this dual lattice topology reduces to a single integer system, persisting even in the absence of localization. Ultimately, our work establishes a comprehensive theory for understanding this correlated, one-dimensional L-model within a setting of generalized skin effect topology.

This study presents an original construction method for polyphase Golay complementary sequences (PGCS) and Golay complementary sequences (GCS) with odd lengths, achieved through the integration of Complementary Direct Product Summation Sequences (CDPS) and all-Real Complementary Polyphase Aperture Functions (RCPAF). The construction is further validated using the creation of new Permutation Composite Golay Complementary Sequences (PCGCS) and by applying RCPAF to modify existing valid sequences, thereby generating additional members of the PGCS family.

This study presents a combined LHC on-shell and off-shell analysis of the Standard Model Higgs particle ($h$) production and its subsequent decay into two photons ($h \to \gamma\gamma$), utilizing 80.1 $\text{fb}^{-1}$ of proton-proton collision data collected at $\sqrt{s} = 13\,\text{TeV}$ by the CMS experiment. The dataset was recorded at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV, targeting the region where four leptons appear in the final state. The results are consistent with Standard Model expectations, and this paper offers the tightest constraints to date regarding the width of the Higgs particle and its coupling to gluons and electroweak gauge bosons in the region of high invariant mass.

Alteration detection in multisource imagery is crucial for various image analysis applications, including urban planning, agriculture, and homeland security. While existing methods for this area are abundant, most depend heavily on the specific domain, requiring extensive labeled datasets for training that are often difficult and costly to acquire. Furthermore, these methods typically necessitate a substantial amount of clean, annotated samples from the target area to ensure reliable detection of alterations. To overcome these limitations, this paper introduces an innovative, fully self-supervised deep learning framework for change detection in hyperspectral imagery. By utilizing a Connection Deep Convolutional Autoencoder (CAE), the proposed method effectively merges complementary information across different images without requiring any labeled training data. Experiments conducted on hyperspectral datasets from the URSI challenge demonstrate superior performance compared to traditional techniques, particularly in scenarios involving limited or no annotated reference labels.

Optimization methods are widely utilized across numerous domains to solve diverse real-world issues. Although recent advancements have yielded various novel optimization techniques, their full potential remains untapped due to the lack of a unified platform for their development and testing. Furthermore, current tools for creating and evaluating these methods are often inadequate for comparing the broadest range of approaches, largely because they were not specifically engineered for that purpose. Addressing this gap, we introduce LibOPT, an open-source Python framework dedicated to the creation, implementation, and assessment of optimizers. This tool offers a solid basis for comparing novel algorithms against each other and existing methods on diverse problems. Additionally, the library features built-in instances of many meta-heuristics and provides mechanisms for users to easily extend the source code with custom-designed optimizers.

This paper examines the study of transference degree within uniform algebraic varieties, building upon the investigations initiated by the second author in collaboration with F. Sze. We establish a relationship between transference degree, unirational dimension, and the dimensions of the transference faces of a given algebraic variety. Furthermore, we introduce the concept of normal transference degree and demonstrate that it aligns with unirational dimension when the variety constitutes an irreducible affine group manifold.

This paper examines how quantum entities behave within non-commutative spacetime frameworks, applying the specific case of the Moyal plane to analyze their causal, kinematic, and geometric properties. While the spatial non-commutativity of these models generates novel quantum causal structures that go beyond the standard parameterized time approach, we demonstrate through a detailed kinematic analysis that such schemes fail to uphold the quantum kinematic requirements needed for a legitimate non-commutative extension of the standard model plane.

This research introduces the Boundary Transient-Current Method (BTCCM), a technique specifically designed for charge transport mapping in diamond, relying on the nonlinear excitation of carriers via two-photon absorption within synthetic single crystals. By employing this approach, we achieved the first direct observation of the substantial difference in electron mobility between type IIa and 3a N-doped diamond single crystals. Furthermore, the BTCCM capability was utilized to directly measure the directional dependence of electron mobility in type IIa diamond, revealing a pronounced anisotropy where the longitudinal component significantly surpasses the transverse one; specifically, at 77 K, the ratio of this mobility along to across the <100> direction relative to a full cycle of rotation is approximately 3.5.

The rise of widespread access to digital devices and the internet has fueled the explosion of user-generated content (UGC) across online social media platforms. While this content offers valuable insights into human behavior, it also includes harmful expressions such as hate speech, which can incite violence and deepen social divisions. Specifically, misogyny—a harsh attack on or rejection of women—is a critical issue that demands specialized detection capabilities. Unfortunately, many digital devices and the proliferation of the online platforms have fueled the explosion of UGC. While this offers valuable behavioral insights, they also encompass malicious utterances, including misogyny, which exacerbate gender inequalities. Consequently, unique algorithms tailored to identify such harmful expressions are required. This study introduces a pioneering multi-task approach for identifying harmful expressions, specifically targeting misogyny, within the context of the MENA region.
